one_month_reasoning: Q3 2026 earnings very likely fall inside the window. As of 2026-10-02 Rambus has not announced a date (a search found no announcement), but its last four reports came on Mondays in the last week of the month, so Oct 26-27 is the likely date [1][13][15]. Guidance is revenue $210-216M, product $110-116M, royalties $69-75M and EPS $0.75-0.82 [1]. The royalty step-down is lumpiness after an elevated Q2, not a trend break, and it lowers the bar for a beat. The skeptic tilt comes from four things: (a) each of the last four prints fell 9-21% the next day (Oct-2025 -8.7%, Feb-2026 -13.4%, Apr-2026 -21.3%, Jul-2026 -9.0%) [16]; (b) the stock is up +39% from its $80.39 close on Sep-14 [16], not the ~30% I said in round 1; (c) the $100M ASR was expected to complete by the end of Q3, so that buyer has most likely left [3]; (d) Q4 guidance will be read through the 2027 DRAM-supply lens. Against that, the guide looks achievable and consensus is 6 Buy / 2 Hold. I use a lognormal with median about $109.5 (about 2% below spot) and a monthly sigma of 20%, slightly under the annual-vol/3.5 rule of thumb of about 23%, because the earnings jump is the main source of variance and it is already priced into that 20%.

Blend about $107, a little below the $111.97 close and below the supervisor's $114.

bear.story: In 2027 RDIMM unit growth falls to single digits as DRAM makers favour HBM, and the MRDIMM ramp slips again behind Diamond Rapids. A large Korea-based licensee renews its royalty at lower terms, inventory gets written down, and the DOJ grand-jury probe produces charges or a settlement that limits licensing practices. EPS of about $3.2 at roughly 21x. I cut this case from 25% because units contracting outright is less likely once unit growth is separated from bit growth.

base.story: Product revenue grows mid-teens, held back by unit supply, with companion chips and MRDIMM helping in late 2027. Royalties stay flat and lumpy. The DOJ matter stays an overhang with no news. NTM EPS of about $3.95 at about 28x.

bull.story: AI inference and agentic workloads lift x86 server builds and memory content. Smaller modules push RCD units well above bit growth, MRDIMM ramps on AMD Venice and then Diamond Rapids, and the DOJ probe closes quietly. EPS of about $4.6 at about 36x, back near the $174 high.

thesis_break_reason: Below about $72 the stock would be about 8% under the $77.89 March 2026 low and about 18x my NTM EPS of $3.95, with about $7/share of net cash. The stock did not go that low even after the -21% April print or the June DOJ/sector selloff. Getting there would most likely need a guided product-revenue decline (RDIMM units actually contracting, or a real RCD share loss), a royalty-renewal shortfall with a top licensee, an inventory write-down, or a DOJ indictment or forced change to licensing practices. That would mean a fundamental break, not 80%-vol noise.

reasoning: Round 2 takes the supervisor's fact-checks on board. (1) My NTM weighting was reversed: the year from Oct-2027 is mostly FY28, which lifts NTM EPS from $3.90 to $3.95, even though I keep FY27 below the unverified $3.72 consensus at $3.55. (2) My FCF base annualized Q2 OCF only. H1 FCF was $123.8M, so the base is about $250-270M, not my implied lower figure. I now deduct about $50M/yr of share-settlement taxes, which is a real skeptic adjustment the supervisor identified but did not apply. (3) The Baird target raise I cited was from 2025. Baird has been Neutral/$120 since the April 2026 downgrade, so I drop it as a positive. (4) My share-loss inference rested only on Trefis and is contradicted by +22% y/y product growth against Montage's ~26%, so I drop it as a multiple input and as a bear driver. (5) The CFO seat is filled and the CAO left without disagreement, so I drop finance turnover as a risk. (6) TrendForce's figure is bit supply, and smaller modules let units grow faster, so outright unit contraction in the bear case is less likely and I cut its probability from 25% to 22%. Points that survive scrutiny: the DOJ grand-jury probe (verified in the 10-Q, no developments, undatable left tail); concentration of about 40% in two customers and 46% in Korea; Baird's 12-15% 2027 unit-growth call; the inventory build; and a four-for-four record of post-earnings drops, now after a +39% rally with the ASR buyer gone. Fair value rises from $103 to about $107, still a little below spot and below the supervisor's $114. I keep that gap because I deduct settlement taxes and do not underwrite the $3.72 consensus. Scenarios: 22% at $68, 53% at $112, 25% at $170, a mean of about $117 with a median near $110. The 12-month ladder is a lognormal with median $110 and sigma 0.58: wide for 80% realized vol, but not the full 80% because two of the biggest moves were one-off earnings gaps. The deep left tail is trimmed slightly for the cash and profitability. The 1-month ladder centres at $109.5 with 20% sigma, a small downside tilt into the print. Research in round 2 was limited to two searches (Q3 date and DOJ updates), both of which found nothing new; supervisor-verified figures are cited to their primary filings.
